extracted.intended_audience: emergency management officials, administrators, trainers, elected/appointed officials, government emergency management agencies, and AHJs responsible for NIMS/ICS implementation and training
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on National Incident Management System (NIMS) components, command structures (ICS, EOC, MAC, JIS), resource management, communications, training curricula, and requirements for jurisdictions to implement NIMS to receive federal preparedness grants. Includes specific course progressions, credentialing/typing guidance, and reporting responsibilities for state/local agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIMS applicability and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Incident Management System (NIMS) provides a common, nationwide approach to enable the whole community to work together to manage all threats and hazards. NIMS applies to all incidents, regardless of cause, size, location, or complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIMS guides all levels of government, NGOs, and the private sector to prevent, protect, mitigate, respond to, and recover from incidents by providing shared vocabulary, systems, and processes aligned with the National Preparedness System.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIMS guiding principles
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMS components are used in accordance with three NIMS guiding principles: Flexibility; Standardization; Unity of Effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility: NIMS is scalable and adaptable to different hazards, geographies, demographics, authorities. Standardization: defines standard organizational structures, standard practices, and common terminology to support interoperability. Unity of Effort: coordinate activities among organizational representatives to achieve common objectives while allowing agencies to maintain authority and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credentialing of personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying and credentialing personnel ensures that the identity and attributes of individuals or team members are validated against an established set of minimum criteria and qualifications for specific job titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the NIMS Guideline for the Credentialing of Personnel to validate identity, qualifications, and attributes for specific job titles; credentialing underpins mutual aid and interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource typing
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource typing is defining and categorizing, by capability, the resources requested, deployed, and used in incidents. Resource typing definitions establish a common language and define a resource's minimum capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIMS resource typing definitions as the common language for mobilization of equipment, teams, and units; resource typing supports capability-based requests and mutual aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Typing Library Tool (RTLT)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RTLT is the online catalogue of all NIMS resource typing definitions and job titles/position qualifications released by FEMA as final publication or interim guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Resource Typing Library Tool for authoritative resource definitions and position qualification information when inventorying, requesting, or deploying resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorying of shareable resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource owners and providers should inventory and maintain current information on their shareable resources using adaptable and scalable inventories that employ interoperable standards for information sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventories can be as simple as a spreadsheet or use IT-based systems; ensure interoperability and scalability so inventories can support mutual aid and operational needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Resource Inventory System (IRIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: IRIS is a distributed, standards-based software tool (provided at no cost by FEMA) that allows users to identify and inventory resources consistently with NIMS resource typing definitions and share information with other agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRIS stores data locally or on a network, supports exchange with other IRIS instances and standards-based systems, and helps match resources to mission needs, capabilities, availability, and response time.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Mutual Aid System
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Mutual Aid System integrates mutual aid across local, intrastate, regional, interstate, tribal, and international boundaries into a unified national system for response to significant incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop written mutual aid agreements across jurisdictions, private sector, NGOs, and whole-community partners to facilitate access to needed resources; use lower levels of mutual aid as building blocks for higher levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Command System (ICS)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICS is a management system enabling effective and efficient domestic incident management through integration of facilities, equipment, personnel, procedures, and communications within a common organizational structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICS is normally structured around six major functional areas: Command; Operations; Planning; Logistics; Intelligence and Investigations; Finance and Administration. It enables incident managers to identify key concerns under urgent conditions without sacrificing attention to command system components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Operations Center (EOC) roles and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: EOCs are locations where staff from multiple agencies come together to address threats and hazards and provide coordinated support to incident command, on-scene personnel, and/or other EOCs; they may be fixed, temporary, or virtual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary EOC functions include collecting, analyzing, and sharing information; supporting resource needs and requests (allocation and tracking); coordinating plans and determining current and future needs; and in some cases providing coordination and policy direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiagency Coordination Group (MAC Group) role
rubrics_metrics.description: MAC Groups (policy groups) are off-site incident management structures composed of agency administrators, executives, or designees from stakeholder agencies and organizations with resources committed to the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MAC Groups make cooperative multiagency decisions, act as policy-level bodies during incidents, support resource prioritization and allocation, and enable decision making among elected/appointed officials and incident managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Information System (JIS) mission and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The JIS integrates incident information and public affairs into a unified organization to provide consistent, coordinated, accurate, accessible, timely, and complete information to the public and stakeholders during incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JIS develops and delivers coordinated interagency messages; creates and executes public information plans and strategies for Incident Commander/Unified Command/EOC director/MAC Group; advises leadership on public affairs issues; and addresses and manages rumors and inaccurate information that could undermine public confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and information management standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications systems need to be interoperable, reliable, scalable, portable, resilient, redundant, and secure to maintain situational awareness and information flow during incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized procedures, protocols, and formats are necessary for gathering, collating, synthesizing, and disseminating incident information regardless of hardware; address incompatible systems and plan for alternate communications when primary systems fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIMS Core Curriculum — purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIMS Training Program identifies courses critical to train personnel capable of implementing all functions of emergency management and develops incident personnel capable of performing necessary functions in their AHJ and assisting with mutual aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training progressions are customized for personnel in ICS, EOC, JIS, and MAC systems and include baseline, supervisory, and advanced/position-specific courses; AHJs should determine which personnel take which courses based on responsibility, incident frequency, and relevant plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training categories for personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: All NIMS training falls into three basic categories: All Incident Personnel; Incident Personnel with Leadership Responsibilities; Incident Personnel Designated as Senior Leaders/Supervisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Incident Personnel: foundational knowledge for nonsupervisory personnel. Leadership Responsibilities: additional background for mid-level personnel establishing initial command or preparing for supervisory roles. Senior Leaders: enhanced knowledge for those designated as ICS/EOC leaders for complex incidents that generate an Incident Action Plan (IAP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline training courses (all personnel)
rubrics_metrics.description: All incident personnel working within ICS/EOC/MAC/JIS/PIO should complete foundational courses including IS-700 NIMS, an Introduction, and IS-100 Introduction to the Incident Command System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These courses introduce NIMS concepts and ICS fundamentals and provide the foundation for higher-level ICS and EOC training.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICS training progression and recommended sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: ICS personnel follow a progression: supervisory personnel should take IS-800, IS-200, then recommended experiential gap before advanced courses (G0191, ICS-300, ICS-400) depending on role; ICS-300 and ICS-400 are for expanding/complex incidents and command/general staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FEMA recommends taking the two-day classroom ICS-200 before ICS-300; do not take ICS-400 immediately after ICS-300—gain additional ICS experience first. AHJs decide required progression based on roles and incident complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: EOC training progression and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: EOC personnel follow a progression with recommended courses including IS-800, IS-2200 (Basic EOC Functions), G0191 (EOC/ICS Interface), and E/L/G2300 (Intermediate EOC Functions) for senior EOC leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FEMA recommends that personnel with EOC leadership responsibilities complete IS-2200 instead of IS-200; AHJs determine how far personnel should progress based on their EOC role and incident complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIS/PIO training progression and courses
rubrics_metrics.description: JIS/PIO personnel should follow a JIS/PIO progression: baseline courses include IS-29 (Public Information Officer Awareness); leadership-focused courses include IS-800 and G0290 (Basic Public Information Officer); advanced leader courses include G0191, E/L/G2300, ICS-300, and ICS-400 depending on EOC/ICS assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AHJs determine progression based on role and incident complexity; some JIS personnel may not progress beyond baseline courses; recommended sequencing (e.g., take ICS-200 before ICS-300) applies where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAC Group training progression and briefings
rubrics_metrics.description: MAC Group (senior officials/executives) baseline training includes G0402/ICS-402: ICS Overview for Senior Officials and a briefing from the emergency management director about jurisdiction threats, hazards, and roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executives and senior officials must understand their roles and responsibilities; a briefing from the emergency management director complements formal course orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: AHJ authority and customization of training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) determines which personnel will take which courses and may require additional advanced training beyond NIMS recommendations for their qualification programs (such as NQS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational leaders should base course assignments on an individual's level of incident responsibility, incident frequency, and organizational emergency management plans; AHJs should coordinate with local and state emergency management agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training vs. full NIMS compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Completing the NIMS Training Program alone does not ensure NIMS compliance; implementation includes adoption and use of ICS, a plain language requirement, inventorying and typing of resources, and other actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations should coordinate implementation efforts with local and state emergency management agencies; compliance for grants requires more than training completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIMS Implementation Objectives and grant eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Local, state, tribal, and territorial jurisdictions are required to adopt NIMS to receive federal Preparedness Grants. The NIMS Implementation Objectives guide jurisdictions in implementation and clarify requirements in FEMA preparedness grant Notices of Funding Opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients and subrecipients of federal preparedness grant awards must achieve, or be actively working to achieve, all NIMS Implementation Objectives to meet grant conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting responsibilities for NIMS compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Services (DHSES) is responsible for reporting New York State's compliance to NIMS to FEMA and gathers compliance information via a short survey from counties, NYC, and state Disaster Preparedness Commission agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictions should respond to state surveys and coordinate with DHSES for questions about NIMS; specific contact addresses are provided for inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor qualifications and instructional standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Integration Center (NIC) develops and reviews NIMS core curriculum courses according to professionally recognized instructional standards, including adherence to adult learning models; the NIC collaborates to define instructor qualifications and required instructor numbers per course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course instructors must deliver materials and activities according to minimum standards in NIMS curriculum instructor guides or course summaries; stakeholders may prescribe stricter instructor qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public information handling best practices (JIS-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: JIS function includes advising incident leadership on public affairs issues, developing interagency messages and public information plans, and addressing/managing rumors and inaccurate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure coordinated, consistent, accurate, accessible, timely messaging across agencies; incorporate rumor management to protect public confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course-specific recommendations and prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: FEMA provides course-specific recommendations such as taking a classroom ICS-200 before ICS-300 and waiting to take ICS-400 until additional ICS experience is gained after ICS-300.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow recommended sequencing and experiential prerequisites to ensure effectiveness of higher-level courses; AHJs may impose additional prerequisites.
